body:
The launch adapter had one validated way to start `claude`: a native Anthropic subscription session. Profiles the catalog marks `hosting: local` are reachable only through the gateway, so the adapter refused them even when the router had recommended them. This change adds the second launch class the catalog 1.6.0 notes describe for `local-code-standard`, so `{claude, local-code-standard}` now launches instead of writing a `.blocked` marker.

What changes:

- `dispatch.sh` gets a gateway-backed launch class beside the native one. It is the native launch plus five per-process variables inside the same `env -i` allowlist: the gateway endpoint, the scoped key, the model pin, the `x-placement` header copied verbatim from the `/v1/place` result fetched for that attempt, and the profile's real context window from the catalog. The `claude` invocation itself is byte-identical to the native one, and the tests check that by comparing the two builders directly.
- The credential is resolved by the terminal at launch time from a 1Password reference in launcher configuration. Only the reference and the service-account env file appear in command text. An empty read stops the launch before `claude` starts, and the generated text opens with `set +x` so an inherited xtrace cannot print the value into the terminal buffer.
- Admission reads the stamp plus the trusted catalog: harness `claude`, the catalog marking the profile local, placement required, no entitlement pool, cost class free. Every other pair keeps refusing with the same wording as before, and a local profile stamped with a vendor pool is refused by name. `codex` and `minimax/strong` are unchanged.
- The readiness library mirrors both classes, and `docs/LIFECYCLE-CONTRACT.md` describes them. `subscriptions.yaml` gains three launcher keys; the endpoint has a default, the credential reference ships empty and is a reference, never a value.
- Tests: a discriminator matrix, an allowlist parsed as a set rather than matched as substrings, a sentinel-based proof that the credential value never reaches command text, titles, logs or any file, four fail-closed preflight cases, and a case that drives an empty credential read through the terminal path and asserts it ends as a launch failure.

Independent review of the branch found no defects in the launch path. It did find that `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable for the moment between the shell expanding the credential and `env` exec'ing `claude`; the record documents that window and names `hidepid=2` on `/proc` as the interim mitigation. Closing it fully means a wrapper shell inside `env -i`, which changes the frozen command shape and belongs to the prox-ops contract, so it is a follow-up there. Other follow-ups: shape-checking the header value (defence in depth, the source is the trusted router) and a shorter timeout for a launch that has printed nothing.

Test results on this host: readiness 279/0, dispatch 250/0, lifecycle 476/0, `run-tests.sh` 332 passed and 1 failed. The one failure is the `lifecycle concurrency gate` aggregate, three timing-sensitive assertions in the operation-lock publication-window scenario that fail identically on pristine `master` at 8a56eb5 on this host, in files this change does not touch.

Size: 6 reviewable files. `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/AFK-PORT-1.4-LV.md` is the change record and is not part of the reviewable diff.

This has not yet been launched against the live gateway; that run is the next change, and it is what upgrades the portability verdict.
title: Add a gateway-backed launch class for local profiles on the claude harness
